content.title: About
content.content: Red seedless grapes are fresh berries of the grapevine (Vitis vinifera) cultivated without seeds. They have a sweet‑tart flavor, crisp texture, and bright red color. Grapes are eaten raw, added to salads, desserts, and juices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Red seedless grapes were developed by breeders in the early 20th century.
Grapevines have been cultivated for over 8,000 years, making them one of the oldest fruit crops.
Seedless varieties are more convenient to eat but contain slightly fewer polyphenols than seeded ones.
A single grapevine can live more than 100 years and produce fruit almost every year.
There are over 5,000 grape varieties, differing in color, taste, and use.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Red grapes contain resveratrol and anthocyanins, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Flavonoids and potassium contribute to lower blood pressure and better vascular function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: One cup (≈150 g) of grapes provides about 100 kcal, making it a good option for weight control.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to grapes.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Grapes are relatively high in natural sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Conventional grapes may carry pesticide residues; washing thoroughly or choosing organic is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat grapes fresh, add them to fruit salads, yogurt, smoothies, desserts, or use them to make juices and cool drinks. They can also be frozen for refreshing summer treats.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store grapes in the refrigerator in their original bag or a ventilated container. When kept properly, they stay fresh for 7–10 days. Remove any spoiled berries to prevent the rest from deteriorating.
